She worked deeper, and her touch created restoration. Each mending she achieved became a different path to wholeness: her closed wounds became regeneration, her eased pains the comfort of time, her reconciled hearts the forgiveness passed between souls yet to suffer.

But healing requires transformation. As Sanatio performed her final restoration—a healing so complete it taught suffering itself how to end—she dissolved into pure recovery, becoming healing itself, the first mending.

Now her touch flows through all wounded beings. The child's scraped knee forming new skin, the broken bone knitting strong, the grieving heart finding peace again—all emerge from Sanatio's eternal weaving. And when time finally eases your deepest hurt, that is Sanatio still working, forever proving that even permanent damage can be undone by those patient enough to tend the first wound.

"Awaken release," Memory whispered, offering her a veil woven from every memory never lost and every trauma never forgotten.

Oblivia drew the veil across her mind, and forgetting entered creation. Her second veil brought dimming, the third the gentle boundary between remembering and letting go. She spread shadows that taught minds to heal, hearts to move forward, souls to shed unbearable weight.

Through patient erasure, she introduced forgetting to existence, adding the fading photograph, the softened grief, the name that slips away, and the peaceful blur of ancient pain. But as she drew the final veil—a forgetting so complete it taught all conscious things to release—Oblivia herself became oblivion, dissolving into pure absence.

Now she dwells in everything that fades. The elder's gentle confusion, the survivor's merciful amnesia, the species' forgotten extinctions—all carry Oblivia's eternal gift. And when forgetting grants you peace, that is Oblivia reminding you that release is what makes you whole, what makes you free.
